samuel2.2.p1.b1.text: Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?

samuel2.2.p1.b3.text: So David went there with his two wives, …

samuel2.2.p1.b4.text: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.

samuel2.2.p2.b1.text: It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.

samuel2.2.p2.b2.text: The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.

samuel2.2.p2.b3.text: … be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.

samuel2.2.p3.b1.text: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim,

samuel2.2.p3.b2.text: and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin—over all Israel.

samuel2.2.p3.b3.text: Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years. The house of Judah, however, followed David.

samuel2.2.p3.b4.text: And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

samuel2.2.p4.b1.text: … met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two camps took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.

samuel2.2.p4.b2.text: Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.

samuel2.2.p4.b4.text: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.

samuel2.2.p5.b1.text: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle,

samuel2.2.p5.b4.text: Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.

samuel2.2.p6.b1.text: Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?

samuel2.2.p6.b2.text: But Asahel refused to turn away; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, … and he fell dead on the spot.

samuel2.2.p6.b3.text: And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.

samuel2.2.p7.b1.text: By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

samuel2.2.p7.b2.text: Must the sword devour forever? … How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?

samuel2.2.p7.b3.text: As surely as God lives, … if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.

samuel2.2.p7.b4.text: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.

samuel2.2.p8.b1.text: And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, … and arrived at Mahanaim.

samuel2.2.p8.b2.text: … he gathered all the troops. In addition to Asahel, nineteen of David’s servants were missing, but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.

samuel2.2.p8.b3.text: Later, they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem.

samuel2.2.p8.b4.text: Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.
